name: TX-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Ellzey's massive financial advantage ($4.7M raised vs $44K)
Incumbency advantage with no polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Ellzey's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge over Minton all point to a comfortable Republican win, and prediction markets price him at 94%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the forecast stays close to fundamentals at roughly R+16.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Minton competitive, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Ellzey, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored in this North Texas district, which leans Republican by about eleven points. He has raised roughly $4.7 million and holds $2.5 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Danny Minton has raised about $44,000. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Ellzey about a 94 percent chance of winning.

The forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap, pointing to a Republican margin in the mid-teens. Minton would need a major, unobserved shift in the political environment to make this competitive.
